name: Haus am Horn
known: Visitor numbers inside are limited for conservation reasons and booking is recommended (Klassik Stiftung Weimar).

name: Kunstmuseum Wolfsburg
known: Directors: Gijs van Tuyl until 2004, Markus Brüderlin from 2006 until his death in 2014, Ralf Beil from 1 February 2015 to December 2018, Andreas Beitin from 1 April 2019 (German Wikipedia;
Hans Dieter Pötsch, chairman of the Volkswagen Group supervisory board, is also chairman of the foundation's board of trustees (e-mobility plus, 24 May 2024).
Volkswagen-funded; director removed 2018 before an oil-themed show.

name: Skulpturenpark Waldfrieden
known: The foundation's board is Tatjana Cragg (chair), Tony Cragg (deputy chair) and Michael Brämer (German Wikipedia).

name: Haus Rabe
known: Oskar Schlemmer designed the interior art, including a four-part metal composition and a five-metre profile head of sheet copper (Vielfalt der Moderne).
The Landkreis Leipzig decided to set up the Kulturstiftung Landkreis Leipzig in 2018, and the Saxon state directorate has recognised it since 30 September 2020.
Board: the imprint lists Frank Rübner (chair), Sophia Littkopf and Franziska Mascheck; the about page lists Frank Rübner, Nina Schreckenbach and Jörn-Heinrich Tobaben.

name: Chale Wote Street Art Festival
known: Founders' account: the founders started with little money, believing the festival "would be transformative" (TRUE Africa, 2015).

name: Gallery 1957
known: Founded by Marwan Zakhem.
Nana Oforiatta-Ayim is creative director (The Art Newspaper, 2016).

name: Nubuke Foundation
known: Tevie is director and Setordji artistic director (Daily Graphic, 15 October 2016).
On the foundation's tenth anniversary in 2016, the founders invited the public to support its mission (Daily Graphic, 15 October 2016).

name: Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art (SCCA Tamale)
known: Founded by the Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama.

name: EMST National Museum of Contemporary Art
known: Established in October 2000 with Anna Kafetsi as founding director.
Directors since: Katerina Koskina (2014 to 2018), interim directors Dimitris Antonakakis and Syrago Tsiara (2019 to 2021), and Katerina Gregos (from 2021) (Wikipedia).
Apollo says only a fraction of the space has been operational since 2015, after "a period of funding shortfalls, administrative problems and difficulties in selecting a permanent director".
2019 governance dispute over the director, not a funding issue.

name: NEON
known: In 2016 NEON paid for the refurbishment of the basement of the Athens Conservatoire, which opened as an 1,800 square metre exhibition space on 24 September 2016 (The Art Newspaper, Anny Shaw, 19 September 2016).
The 2016 Athens Conservatoire basement refurbishment cost 180,000 euros (The Art Newspaper, 2016).
The source of the founder's money: from 1983 to 2007 Daskalopoulos was principal owner, chairman and CEO of Delta Holdings/Vivartia, described by Wikipedia as Greece's largest food conglomerate.
He now chairs DAMMA Holdings SA, a financial services and investment company (NEON website, Wikipedia).

name: National Gallery - Alexandros Soutzos Museum
known: Founded by law on 10 April 1900, with Georgios Iakovidis as its first chief curator (gallery site).
A public law entity run by a nine-member board; the Minister of Culture appoints the Director.
Its structure page names the board of directors; its footer links to the Diavgeia register.

name: Onassis Stegi
known: Origin of the founder's money: Aristotle Onassis "amassed the world's largest privately owned shipping fleet";

name: State of Concept Athens
known: Founded in 2013 by the art critic and curator iLiana Fokianaki, who is its founding director (State of Concept website).

The website's home page states: "State of Concept's physical space in Athens is permanently closed." The team page lists Fokianaki as founding director and Konstantina Melachrinou as production manager and press officer.

name: TAVROS
known: Founded by locus athens, Maria-Thalia Carras and Olga Hatzidaki.
